name: ESTONIA

flag.title: The Tricolour
flag.note: Blue, black & white — sky, soil, snow

lead: Estonia sits on the Baltic Sea. It has 2,000+ islands, fairy-tale towns and spooky bogs. It was first to hold online elections, and almost everything now runs digitally. Singing festivals gather a quarter of the nation.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Forest covers more than half of Estonia. Ancient bogs spread for miles, with dark, still water. The coast has more than 2,200 islands.
Saaremaa, the biggest island, has Kaali, a lake in a meteor crater. A space rock punched into the rock there 3,500 years ago.
animals: Wolves, brown bears, lynxes and elk roam Estonia's forests. White-tailed eagles soar over coastal wetlands. Every spring, thousands of cranes gather in the bogs.
White storks nest on rooftop poles in villages. Estonians think they are lucky.
culture: Every five years, the Song Festival draws up to 100,000 performers. When 30,000 voices join, the sound carries for kilometres. It helped Estonia keep its identity through decades of foreign rule.
Sauna is a national ritual shared with family and friends. Skype was built here, and children learn to code (write computer programs) from age seven.
history: Danes, Germans, Swedes and Russians all ruled Estonia. Estonians kept their language and songs every time. German merchants built the cone-topped towers of Tallinn, the capital, in the 13th century.

In 1991, Estonia broke free from the Soviet Union, a giant Russian-led state, and built a digital state. In 2005 it held the world's first official internet election. Today 'e-Residency' lets anyone start an Estonian company online.
wows: Estonia has more meteorite craters (holes from space rocks) per km² than almost any other country.
Estonian engineers built the video-call app Skype in Tallinn and launched it in 2003.
Estonia held the world's first legally binding (official) national internet election in 2005.
Citizens can register a company online in minutes, because government is almost fully digital.
UNESCO lists the Estonian Song Festival among humanity's living traditions.
More than half of Estonia is forest, one of Europe's highest shares.
In 1989, Estonians joined a 675 km human chain across three Baltic states to demand freedom.

myths.fact: Scandinavia means Norway, Sweden and Denmark. Estonia is Baltic, like Latvia and Lithuania.
Wolves howl to talk to each other. The moon has nothing to do with it.
